get.summary: The Server's version, its library, the machine it runs on and the state of its Worker.
The person's settings the Server acts on, as their preferences file has them.

put.summary: Changes the person's settings, and keeps them in their preferences file.

get.summary: The viewport: its mesh, camera and size. Frames come over the /ws/viewport WebSocket.

put.summary: Shows a mesh file in the viewport.

delete.summary: Takes the mesh and whatever it wears off the viewport.

put.summary: Moves the viewport's camera.

post.summary: What is under a position in the viewport, and the camera a stroke there carries.

put.summary: Puts a stack on its mesh in the viewport, which shows every stroke from then on.
Lays pictures over the mesh's own materials. An empty body takes them off.
Sets how the model is lit, shown and finished: environment, light, exposure, curve, look, view, lens and effects. No export sees any of it.

post.summary: Writes the picture the viewport shows now to a PNG on the Server's machine, with its camera, display settings and look, at the size asked for or the one clients asked for.

put.summary: Draws only some named meshes and materials (texture sets) of the model, for every client. Empty lists draw the whole model.
Shows a finished bake's normal and occlusion maps on the mesh it was baked onto.
Lays a bake's setup over the model before it runs: where its rays start and how far they reach, the high meshes see-through, and which parts match by name. An empty low mesh takes it off.

get.summary: The bake setup the viewport shows, and the key to its colours.

put.summary: Lays a graph's Output nodes over the mesh, or the display's shape with none, as they stand now, or shows one node's picture there. Ask again to see a later edit.

get.summary: A node's preview as a PNG, by the hash an event carried. It never changes, so cache it for ever.
Every preset this library can use: the factory ones and those in shared/export-presets.
The Server's library: its settings, its size and whether a rescan is running.
One page of projects: by name, or by relevance when searching. `folder` keeps those directly in it.

post.summary: Writes a new project's files. It reaches the listings once the index has caught up.
Copies a shipped compound into the library as a file, so that it can be edited.
Writes a new, empty graph file. It reaches the listings once the index has caught up.

get.summary: One page of the tags on projects, by name, with how many projects carry each.
One page of shared assets with their usage counts: by name, or by relevance when searching.
One page of the tags on shared assets, by name, with how many assets carry each.
What saving a shared asset would touch: its dependent projects, and how many are pinned.
The folders directly in a folder, where no parent is the top of the library.

post.summary: Makes a folder.

patch.summary: Renames a folder or changes its colour. Nothing in it may be open to rename it.

delete.summary: Deletes a folder, never a project: `lift` moves what it holds up a level first.

post.summary: Moves folders and projects into a folder, all of them or none. Nothing moved may be open.

get.summary: What a project holds. Read from its folder, so it works before the index has caught up.

patch.summary: Gives a project a new display name. Its folder stays.

delete.summary: Moves a project to the library's hidden trash.

post.summary: Brings a mesh into a project, and its detailed mesh if it has one.

get.summary: Whether a mesh file differs from the one the project already has, so that reloading has work to do.

The facts of a mesh file: one below the library, as a project lists it, or any file on this machine, so a
client can say what a mesh is before it is brought in.

put.summary: Keeps what an export of the whole library is set to in library.yaml, where any client's next library export starts. GET /library reads it back.
Keeps what a project's export is set to in its project.yaml, where any client's next export starts.
Keeps how a project's bakes run, which texture sets they make maps for and the files they read beyond its mesh, in the project's own file.
Keeps how the viewport is to open in a project, in its project.yaml. It is kept, not shown: PUT /viewport/display shows it.

Keeps what a project's texture sets are held to before export in its project.yaml: a GPU memory budget, a size limit and a texel density, which GET /stacks/{id}/checks and the texel density view measure against.
Keeps how a project's painting was left, in its project.yaml: the colours strokes last used, its palette, the brush and the symmetry, so they survive a restart and any client starts from them.

patch.summary: Sets a project's mesh, detailed mesh and auto unwrap. A mesh goes under all its texturing documents.

post.summary: Makes a document of a kind in a project.
Brings a mesh or a picture into a project. Anything else is refused.
Brings a picture into a project, for a layer or a mask to read.

get.summary: A picture the library holds, as its file: what a client shows of a projection or a stencil it frames.

patch.summary: Puts a texturing document on another mesh of its project.

delete.summary: Moves a document to the library's bin, with the paint it keeps beside it. It may not be open.

patch.summary: Says what a graph is for: a material, a mask, a brush or a filter.

post.summary: Makes a new document with another's content, as Save As and Duplicate do.

get.summary: Whether a document has work autosaved after its last save.

post.summary: Restores or forgets autosaved work. The document has to be closed.
Copies a project beside itself, with identities of its own.

get.summary: What a project's layers can be filled with. A search keeps those with every word in their name, tags, type, kind, origin, project or path, wherever they are from.

post.summary: Makes a material graph ready for a project's layers, and names it for them.
Renders a graph to a picture in its project, which a brush can stamp.
Brings a project's layers up to edits saved in the graphs they read.

get.summary: The brush and tool presets a project can use: the shipped ones, its own and other projects', favourites first.

post.summary: Saves a brush as a new preset, a document of the project.

put.summary: Rewrites a preset: from the brush as it stands, or as a favourite or not. A shipped preset keeps a copy in the project instead.

get.summary: What publishing a saved graph as a package would bring: its project's compounds, the shipped ones it reads, its pictures, and anything that stops it, with what compiling it said.

post.summary: Publishes a saved graph as a package in the library's packages folder, replacing one of its name. Every project's shelf then offers it.
Pictures of documents, projects or shelf materials, by hash under /previews, drawing those the cache lacks first. A project is drawn as the document that best stands for it.

patch.summary: Sets every tag a project has, in its project.yaml.
Gives a document a new display name. Its file stays.
Sets every tag a document has, in its project's project.yaml.
Pins a project's reference to an asset at the bytes it has now, or lets it follow the asset again.

get.summary: What the library's bin holds: deleted projects and documents, the latest first.

delete.summary: Deletes everything in the bin for good.

post.summary: Puts something back where it was deleted from. A project whose folder was taken comes back beside it.

delete.summary: Deletes one thing in the bin for good.

get.summary: The library's cache folder and how much room it takes. Deleting it costs only time.
The open graphs.

post.summary: Opens a graph file, or joins the session that has it open, and starts evaluating it.

get.summary: The whole document, its undo history and the newest previews.

delete.summary: Ends a session. Unsaved edits refuse this unless discard is set.

get.summary: Every node this graph can use, with ports and settings, for a palette.
The nodes this graph can use, best match first. takes and gives keep those a wire of that kind can use.
The compounds this graph can hold, and the path that opens the graph behind each.

post.summary: Saves some nodes as a new compound beside the graph and holds it in their place, as one undo step.
Applies a batch of edits, whole or not at all, as one undo step.
Takes back the newest batch, whichever client sent it.
Puts back the newest undone batch.

get.summary: The undo history as a list, for a client that shows it.

post.summary: Undoes or redoes until a step is the newest that stands, as one event.
Writes the document to its file. A file changed on disk refuses this unless force is set.
Evaluates again, which also rewrites previews a deleted cache has lost.
Writes a node's picture at the size the graph computes it. /previews/{hash} serves the PNG.

put.summary: Chooses the folder of baked maps this graph's Mesh Map nodes read, and remembers it beside the file.

get.summary: The events after a number. /ws/graphs/{id}?since= sends the same events as they happen.

Checks the texture set before export, against its project's budget, size limit, texel density and export preset, and its layout and values against what a mesh and a physical material can have. Each problem has a stable code and where it is.

post.summary: Saves layers, or one layer's mask, into a project as a smart material or smart mask its shelf offers.

A picture of a brush: one stroke of it at a size of its own, white on nothing, its pressure rising and falling, drawn by the Worker under /previews with the alphas this stack's strokes read. A brush no stroke could take is refused with its reason.
What every channel holds at a place on the map, as a material picker takes it up: one texel of each, read back from the composite at full size, as numbers.

get.summary: The open stacks.

post.summary: Opens a layer stack, or joins the session that has it open.

get.summary: The blend modes, filters, mask sources, generators, mesh maps and brush alphas a stack can name.

post.summary: Writes a new stack with a base and a paint layer, and opens it.

get.summary: The whole stack, its history and the newest maps.

delete.summary: Ends a session. Unsaved edits refuse this unless discard is set.

post.summary: Applies a batch whole or not at all, as one undo step. A stroke is a list of stamps, never pixels.
Copies layers with their pixels as they stand, for a pasteLayers command in this stack or another.
Takes back the newest batch, whichever client sent it.
Puts back the newest undone batch.

get.summary: The undo history as a list, for a client that shows it.

post.summary: Undoes or redoes until a step is the newest that stands, as one event.
Writes the pixels and then the stack. A file changed on disk refuses this unless force is set.

put.summary: Chooses the bake its generators and bake masks read.

post.summary: Composites again, which also rewrites maps a deleted cache has lost.

get.summary: The colours of the id map the stack reads, the largest first, and the one at a place on it if asked.
What a node or compound this stack can run takes: its numbers, its settings and the images it reads, by port. The project's own compounds are included, which the vocabulary's lists are not.

post.summary: The layer on top at a place on the map, as a click on the mesh or the map finds it. Its answer is a layer id: the Worker weighs each layer there and no picture leaves it.

get.summary: Each fill drawn alone and small, under /previews. A layer that has not changed is not drawn again.
A digest of each map as it stands, the same one an export reports, with no pixels in the reply.
The named meshes in the stack's texture set, which a layer can be limited to.

post.summary: Draws where some named meshes lie in the layout, as a picture for a setLayer command's meshMask.
Evaluates from nothing and writes each map to a file, and says where and what they hold.

get.summary: The events after a number. /ws/stacks/{id}?since= sends the same events as they happen.
Every job the Server remembers, newest first, and the sequence to follow from.

post.summary: Queues a bake, or answers from the cache when the same bake has been made.

get.summary: One job.

post.summary: Asks a job to stop. A running job stops at the end of its row of the atlas.

get.summary: The events after a number. /ws/jobs?since= sends the same events as they happen.
An 8-bit PNG of one map of a finished bake.

post.summary: What a build would do, from build keys alone. Nothing runs, and nothing is written.
Queues a build. It follows as a job, and survives its Worker and the Server.

get.summary: What a build did to the library, as far as it has got.
One page of what a finished build did to each project, with the paths of what it wrote.
A preset as its file says it, where it comes from, and its text.

put.summary: Keeps a preset as a file in the library's or a project's export-presets, renaming one if asked.

delete.summary: Removes a library's or a project's preset file. A factory preset cannot be removed.

post.summary: What a preset would be and the files it would write for a project, keeping nothing.
Brings a preset file into the library's or a project's export-presets, after reading it.
A region of one exported file as the file holds it, beside its source, with the error per lane.

get.summary: One picture of a compression preview as a PNG: source, written or difference.

projects.description: The projects that depend on the asset, directly or through other assets.

pinned.description: How many of Projects a pin holds back; the rest rebuild.

unreadableDocuments.description:
Project and asset documents the index could not read. They may depend on the asset too, so a value above zero
means the counts are a lower bound.

items.description: One page of the dependent projects.

offset.description: The offset the page starts at.

limit.description: The most items a page holds.

AssetImpact.description: What saving a shared asset would touch: "affects 412 projects, 3 pinned" (plan §5).

total.description: How many assets match, on all pages.

offset.description: The offset the page starts at.

limit.description: The most items a page holds.

path.description: The asset's file, below the library, with forward slashes.

revision.description: The content hash of the asset's file, or null when the file is missing.

usageCount.description: How many projects reference the asset directly.

AssetSummary.description: One document other projects can use, as the browser shows it.

intervalSeconds.description: How often open, unsaved documents are kept at the most. Zero is off.

idleSeconds.description:
How long after the last edit a document is kept, without waiting for the interval. Zero
waits.

keep.description: How many autosaves of a document are kept, the latest first. Restoring takes the latest.

AutosavePreferences.description: How unsaved work is kept. It goes to the library's cache, never over a document.

source.description:
`auto`: the high mesh's vertex colours, else its materials. `vertex-colour`; `material`, each
            material's base colour and base colour picture; or `texture`, the picture at string BakeColourOptions.Texture
            read at the high mesh's own coordinates, which moves any map from one UV layout to another.

texture.description: For `texture`: the picture to carry across, as a path on the Server's machine.

BakeColourOptions.description: Where a colour map's colour comes from.

path.description: The file.

scale.description:
What a stored unit value is multiplied by to get the measurement back, for a signed map in an integer format;
zero when there is nothing to undo.

BakedMapFile.description: One baked map, as a file.

range.description:
`measured`, the largest height found; `rays`, the longer ray distance; or `custom`,
            double BakeHeightOptions.Scale. The last two are the same for every bake made with them, so their maps agree.

scale.description: The range for `custom`, in the rays' units.

source.description:
`auto`: vertex colours, else materials when there are several, else connected shells. Or one of
            `material`, `material-colour` (each material's base colour), `vertex-colour`, `mesh`
            (each named part) and `shell`.

palette.description: How labels become colours: `random`, `hue` or `grey`. Colours stay colours.

BakeIdOptions.description: What an ID map labels, and how it colours the labels.

rays.description: How many rays a texel's occlusion is estimated with.

distance.description: How far an occluder counts, in the rays' units.

spread.description: The half-angle of the cone the rays fill, in degrees: 90 is the hemisphere.

falloff.description: How an occluder counts for less further away: `none`, `linear` or `smooth`.

distribution.description: How the rays are spread: `cosine` or `uniform`.

minimum.description: How near an occluder may be and not count, in the rays' units.

ignoreBackfaces.description: Whether a ray passes through the back of a face.

withinPart.description: Whether only the texel's own part occludes it, when parts are matched by name.

groundPlane.description: Whether a floor under the high mesh occludes too. Y is up.

groundOffset.description: How far above the high mesh's lowest point the floor is, in the rays' units.

BakeOcclusionOptions.description: The occlusion rays, which ambient occlusion, the bent normal and thickness share.

supersampling.description: How many samples along each side of a texel.

gutter.description: How many texels of dilation surround each chart.

maps.description:
Which maps to write: `normal`, `height`, `ao`, `bent`, `curvature`,
`thickness`, `position`, `world`, `id`, `colour`. The default is what a project's
masks read.

space.description: The frame of the normal and bent normal maps: `tangent` or `object`.

rays.description: How far the rays look and what they may strike, which every map rests on.

occlusion.description: The occlusion rays, which ambient occlusion, the bent normal and thickness share.

id.description: What the ID map labels and how it colours them.

rounding.description: Edges baked round into the normal, with no high poly to give them a bevel.

colour.description: Where the colour map's colour comes from.

BakeOptions.description:
How a bake runs, with no meshes in it: what a project keeps between bakes and every client sends. Each map's
own settings are a part of their own.

name.description: The name both sides share once their endings are gone.

lowFaces.description: The low mesh's faces of that name, zero for a high part no low part matched.

highFaces.description: The high mesh's faces of that name, zero for a low part that matched nothing.

BakePreviewPart.description:
One part name as matching by name sees it: how many faces each side has and the colour it is drawn
in.

oneOf.description: What was asked for, or null when the preview is off.

parts.description:
The parts by name, in the low mesh's order and then the high's, when parts are matched by name; empty when
they are not.

warnings.description: What the preview left out or could not read.

BakePreviewState.description: What the viewport shows of a bake's setup: the key to its colours, and what it could not show.

front.description: How far a ray looks outward, in front of the low mesh.

rear.description: How far a ray looks inward, behind the low mesh, or past it from a cage.

units.description:
What the distances here and in BakeOcclusionOptions are in: `relative`, fractions of the
high mesh's bounding-box diagonal, or `absolute`, the model's own units.

ignoreBackfaces.description: Whether a ray passes through a high face turned away from the low mesh's facing.

skew.description: How far rays lean from the smoothed direction towards the low mesh's own normal, 0 to 1.

skewMap.description: A grey image saying where to apply the skew, or empty for everywhere.

distanceMap.description:
A grey image correcting how far the rays reach over the atlas, or empty for as set: mid grey leaves them,
black pulls them onto the low mesh and white sends them twice as far, front, rear and cage alike.

matchByName.description: Whether a part of the low mesh only strikes the high part of the same name.

lowSuffix.description: What a low part's name ends in, which matching by name takes off.

highSuffix.description: What a high part's name ends in, which matching by name takes off.

BakeRayOptions.description: How far a bake's rays look from the low mesh, and what they may strike.

high.description: The detailed meshes, in order: one is usual, and a model split across files lists them all.

low.description: The mesh baked onto, which must have texture coordinates.

output.description: The folder the maps are written to.

cage.description: A mesh with the low mesh's faces, moved outward, which the rays start from.

material.description: The material of the low mesh to bake, for one texture set of a model that has several.

uvSet.description:
The low mesh's texture coordinate set the maps are baked in, by the file's number: zero for the first
(#210). Null bakes a texture set in the set it is laid out in, when the low mesh is a project's and
string? BakeRequest.Material names one of its texture sets, and in the first otherwise. The high mesh is read
whole, so its sets do not matter, but for a picture moved from its layout, which is always its first.

name.description: The stem of each file's name, or null for the low mesh's.

options.description: What to bake and how: the part a project keeps between bakes.

BakeRequest.description:
A high-to-low bake. Everything is a path on the Server's machine, and the results are files there: a client
sends paths and gets paths, whichever client it is (plan §8).

covered.description: How many texels held chart content.

missed.description: How many found no source and took the closest point instead.

warnings.description: What could not be baked as asked.

cached.description: Whether this was found in the cache and nothing ran.

log.description: What the bake read and found, line by line: the meshes, each part's match, the time it took.

enabled.description: Whether edges are rounded at all.

width.description: How far either side of an edge the bevel reaches, in the rays' units.

edges.description:
Which edges: `angle`, every edge whose faces meet at double BakeRoundingOptions.Angle or more, or `hard`, the
edges the mesh's own normals split, which is the nearest a mesh file has to an edge weight.

angle.description: For `angle`: the least angle between two faces that is an edge, in degrees.

BakeRoundingOptions.description: Edges baked round into the normal map, the bevel a hard-surface model was not modelled with.

normalised.description: Whether the map is divided by its largest value, so the thickest texel reads white.

count.description: How many entries went for good.

id.description: The entry, which the bin routes take.

name.description: Its display name when it was deleted.

from.description: Where it lived, below the library, and where restoring puts it.

BinItem.description: Something in the library's bin, which can be put back or deleted for good.

bytes.description: The room they take on disk.

path.description: Below the library: a project's folder, or a document's file.

BinRestored.description: Where something put back from the bin now is.

tool.description: What the pointer does: brush, eraser, line or path.

brush.description: The brush, its size among it.

colour.description: The colour it paints, as `#rrggbb`, or null to keep the colour chosen.

favourite.description: Whether it is one of the favourites, which a shelf shows first.

BrushPreset.description:
A brush or tool preset: what the pointer paints as and with. It is a document of a project, a `.ptbrush`
file, and the file is the truth.

name.description: What to call it, which names its file.

preset.description: What it holds: usually the brush as it stands.

BrushPresetCreateRequest.description: The body of `POST /api/v1/library/brushes`, which saves a new preset in a project.

source.description: What names it to the routes: `starter:` and a name, or its file's path in the library.

project.description: The project it lives in, when that is another one.

items.description: Them, favourites first, then by origin and name.

BrushPresetList.description: The presets a project can use: the shipped ones, its own, and other projects'.

project.description: The project a shipped preset's copy goes in.

source.description: Which preset, as the shelf names it.

BrushPresetUpdateRequest.description:
The body of `PUT /api/v1/library/brushes`, which rewrites a preset: from the brush as it stands, or to make
it a favourite or not. A shipped preset cannot change, so changing one keeps a copy in the project instead.

rebuilds.description: Outputs with no result under their current key, counted once per project.

shared.description: How many of those are the same work as another's, because their keys are equal.

pinned.description: Outputs that read the asset through a pin that holds them still.

unresolved.description: Outputs that cannot be built: a missing input, an unreadable reference.

nothing.description: Why a build would write nothing, or null when it would write something.

items.description: One page of the projects, by name.

offset.description: The offset the page starts at.

limit.description: The most items a page holds.

BuildPreview.description:
What a build would do, from the build keys and with nothing run. int BuildPreview.Rebuilds and
int BuildPreview.Pinned are exact for outputs, where the asset's impact counts every project that references it at
all. An asset a project references and no output reads is in neither.

path.description: Its path below `projects/`.

outputs.description: The outputs that would be made.

exports.description: The exports that would be written.

BuildPreviewProject.description: What a build would do for one project.

asset.description: Only what reads this shared asset, directly or not. Null for the whole library.

projects.description: Only these projects. Null or empty for all of them.

presets.description:
The presets to export through. Null means the library's `exportTargets`; empty, no
export.

folder.description: Where exports go, or null for `exports/` in the library.

oneOf.description: The presets' settings changed for this export, or null for the presets as they are.

path.description: The folder.

bytes.description: The room it takes on disk.

CacheInfo.description: The library's cache: what deleting it would cost is time, and nothing else.

severity.description: `error` stops an engine taking it; `warning` needs a look.

values.description: The numbers and names the sentence was written from, by name.

CheckProblem.description: One problem a texture set has before it is exported.

view.description: A viewport view that shows it, one of IReadOnlyList<string> ViewportViews.All, or null.

oneOf.description: A camera that looks at it on the mesh, or null where it is no place on the mesh.

u.description: A texture coordinate across where it is, or null.

v.description: A texture coordinate down where it is, or null.

setting.description:
The project's setting that decides it, as `block.field` (`checks.memoryBudget`,
`export.preset`), or null.

CheckTarget.description: Where a problem is, for a client to go to it.

psnr.description: Peak signal-to-noise ratio in decibels, or null where nothing changed.

maxError.description: The largest difference, in the file's numbers from 0 to 1.

CompressionLaneError.description: How far one lane of a file is from what it was made from.

id.description: The preview, by the hash of what it was made from, for its pictures.

levels.description: How many levels the file has.

region.description: The region shown, as x, y, width and height in the level's texels.

gain.description: What the difference picture's errors are multiplied by.

bytes.description:
What the whole file takes in GPU memory as written, by the measure the pre-export checks use
(`texture-over-budget`).

uncompressed.description: What the same file would take with no block compression, by the same measure.

CompressionPreviewInfo.description:
What a file's encoding does to a region of it. The pictures are not in this: each is a PNG at
`GET /api/v1/export/compression/{id}/{picture}`, for `source`, `written` and `difference`.

set.description: The texture set, or null for the project's first.

oneOf.description: The export's changes, as a build would be sent them: another compression, size or quality.

x.description: Where the region is centred across the level, from 0 to 1.

y.description: Where the region is centred down the level, from 0 to 1.

side.description: The region's largest side in texels, 4 to 512.

CompressionPreviewRequest.description:
The body of `POST /api/v1/export/compression` (#217): one file of an export, to see a region of it as the
file holds it beside what it was made from.

saved.description: When it was kept, or null when there is nothing to recover.

DocumentRecovery.description: Whether a document has work autosaved after its last save.

path.description: The document, below the library.

restore.description: True puts it in place of the file, and false forgets it.

DocumentRecoveryRequest.description: What to do with autosaved work, with the document closed.

enabled.description: Whether it is written at all.

format.description: Another format for it, or null for the preset's.

compression.description:
What a KTX2 or DDS file holds: none, half, float or bc1 to bc7. Null keeps the preset's, which a plain file
made a container takes as none.

quality.description: For JPEG, 1 to 100; for BC6H and BC7, fast, balanced or best. Null keeps the preset's.

mips.description: Whether a KTX2 or DDS file carries a mip chain. Null keeps the preset's.

ExportFileChoice.description: One file of a preset changed for one export.

preset.description: The preset it is a file of.

format.description: The format it is written in.

compression.description: What a KTX2 or DDS file holds, or null for the preset's.

quality.description: For JPEG, 1 to 100; for BC6H and BC7, fast, balanced or best. Null for the preset's.

mips.description: Whether a KTX2 or DDS file carries a mip chain, or null for the preset's.

ExportFileSetting.description: One preset file as a project's export last had it.

label.description: Its name for a person, with its depth.

linear.description: Whether it holds only linear numbers, as a float or 16-bit format does here.

container.description: Whether it is a GPU container, the only kind a preset can block-compress.

ExportFormatInfo.description: A file format a preset or an export can name.

size.description: The longest side of every file, 1 to 8192: 2048 makes a 4096 map's file 2048.

filter.description: How a file changes size: box, bilinear or nearest.

it. The graph's own file holds its parameters, presets and what it says about itself, so this repeats none of
them.

What a project keeps about baking, in its own file: the options, which texture sets to bake, and the files
beyond the project's mesh that a bake reads.

The texel density the sets are held to, in texels per unit of the model (a metre in glTF), or zero for the
library's.

ProjectCheckSettings.description:
What a project holds its texture sets to before they are exported (#159), kept in its `project.yaml`. A
zero is no limit, and a texel density of zero is the library's.

checks.description: What its texture sets are held to now.

unwrap.description: How Auto Unwrap lays a mesh out.

bake.description: How its bakes run, which texture sets they make maps for, and what they read beyond its mesh.

How its painting was left: recent colours, palette, brush and symmetry, or null for none yet.

What its texture sets are held to before export: a memory budget, a size limit, a texel density. Null holds

export starts from next time. Any client reads and writes them; a build reads only what a request sends, so

Whether a mesh with no UV layout is given one, in a new file beside it. True also applies it to the mesh the
project has now.

preservePaint.description:
Whether paint moves to a new mesh's layout, by where it sits on the surface. Open documents have to be closed
first, as it rewrites their paint files.

oneOf.description:
How Auto Unwrap lays a mesh out. A mesh it already wrote is unwrapped again with these, from the file it came
from, and its paint moves across as a new mesh's would.

reassign.description:
For a new mesh whose materials are not the old one's (#89): which of the new materials each texture set on an
old material that the new mesh lacks becomes, by name. The set keeps its layers, its paint (moved across with
Preserve Paint) and its bake folder's name changes with it. A set left out, or sent to a material another set
holds, stays as it is, and a new material no set takes gets a set of its own.

How the viewport is to open in this project from now on. It is kept, not applied: `PUT /viewport/display`
shows it.

ServerPreferences.description:
The Server's settings that belong to the person and not to a library or project, kept in a plain file beside
the discovery file, which anyone can read and edit.

layer.description: The id of the layer that publishes it.

uses.description: Who reads it, and in which channel.

StackAnchor.description: An anchor point and every place that reads it.

channel.description: The channel read, by usage. Empty, for a fill or a filter's input only, means the channel being written.

StackAnchorRef.description: A reference to an anchor point, by its name, in one channel.

layer.description: The id of the layer that reads it.

where.description: What part of that layer: fill, mask, mask entry 2, or an input's port.

channel.description: The channel it reads, or empty for the channel being written.

StackAnchorUse.description: One place a stack reads an anchor point.

radius.description:
In SizeSpace: by default texels for a stroke with no view and the units of the picture for
one with a view. Above zero and at most float StackBrushes.MaximumRadius.

flow.description: How much one stamp lays down, 0 to 1.

opacity.description: How much a whole stroke can lay down, 0 to 1.

spacing.description: How far apart stamps are, as a share of the radius: above zero, and above 2 leaves gaps.

falloff.description: How soft its edge is, 0 to 1.

alpha.description: A named alpha (Round, Square, Chisel, Cross) or an image relative to the stack, or null.

positionJitter.description: How far a stamp strays, as a share of the radius, 0 to 1.

angleJitter.description: How far a stamp turns either way, in radians.

sizeJitter.description: How much of its radius a stamp can lose, 0 to 1.

pressureSize.description: How much of the radius pressure takes off, 0 to 1.

pressureFlow.description: How much of the flow pressure takes off, 0 to 1.

lazy.description:
How far the brush trails the pointer, in the units of the radius: a lazy mouse. 0 follows it. A line or a path
takes none, so that it reaches its last point.

curve.description: How its edge falls away: smooth, linear, spherical or tip.

aspect.description:
How much longer than wide a stamp is, 1 to 16; 1 is round. It keeps the area of the round stamp, so a longer one
is narrower.

aspectAngle.description: Which way the long side points, in radians, on the picture or the map it is made on.

flowJitter.description: How much of its flow a stamp can lose, 0 to 1.

scatterAxis.description: Which way PositionJitter moves a stamp: both, or across the stroke only.

accumulate.description:
Whether stamps build up where they overlap, to the opacity. Off, a place keeps the strongest stamp to reach it,
so a slow drag paints what a fast one does.

sizeSpace.description:
What the radius is measured in: `screen`, the stroke's own picture or map; `texture`, texels of the
map whatever the view; or `model`, thousandths of the model's size (its bounds' diagonal), which needs a
mesh. A size other than screen is measured where the stroke starts and kept for the whole of it.

occlusion.description:
Whether a stroke with a view paints only what its camera sees. Off, every texel within the depth under the brush
is painted, hidden or not: a face close under a strap, the inside of a lip.

occlusionTolerance.description:
How far in front of a texel something may lie and still not hide it, in thousandths of the model's size (its
bounds' diagonal), 0 to 1000: a decal floating a hair over a face is not the face's occluder.

facing.description:
How far a face may turn from the camera and still be painted, in radians from the line of sight, 0 to π/2. π/2
paints every face the camera looks at; less keeps a stroke with a view off the faces it only grazes, where a
stamp smears into a streak. Measured per triangle.

resume.description:
Whether a stroke that starts where the last one stopped carries it on. A client that sees one start there sends
where the brush stood as IReadOnlyList<float>? StackStroke.Resume; the brush only says whether to.

StackBrush.description: A brush. Everything but the radius has the value a new brush has.

hash.description: Its name in the preview cache, or null when the brush draws nothing.

StackBrushPreview.description: A picture of a brush: a stroke of it drawn small, under `/previews/{hash}`.

default.description: A new brush, which Reset to Default goes back to.

falloffs.description: How an edge can fall away.

sizeSpaces.description: What a radius can be measured in.

scatterAxes.description: Which way scatter can move a stamp.

axes.description: The axes a symmetry can use.

centres.description: What a symmetry's plane or axis can pass through.

tools.description: What a preset can hold the pointer as.

fills.description: How much of a mesh one click of a polygon fill can take.

maximumRadius.description: The largest radius a stroke takes, in its own units.

maximumAspect.description: The longest a stamp can be, against its width.

maximumCount.description: The most strokes a radial symmetry makes.

materialProjections.description: How a material brush can lay its maps on the mesh.

StackBrushTerms.description: What a brush's fields take and how a new brush starts, so a client keeps no list or default of its own.

usage.description: Its usage: baseColor, roughness and so on.

set.description: The texture set, or empty for a model with no named sets.

texelDensity.description: Texels per unit of the model across the whole set, or zero where it has no area.

targetDensity.description: What the project holds it to, or zero for nothing.

memoryBytes.description: The GPU memory its exported files take with the project's preset, mips included.

memoryBudget.description: The project's budget in bytes, or zero for none.

problems.description:
What is wrong, in the order of IReadOnlyList<string> CheckCodes.All, which puts the project's limits, the errors,
first.

StackChecks.description: The reply to `GET /api/v1/stacks/{id}/checks`: one texture set measured against its project.

id.description: What a paste names it by. A Server that restarts has none.

layers.description: How many layers it holds at the top.

StackClip.description: Layers copied out of a stack, which a StackPasteLayers names.

layers.description: Which. A layer inside another of them goes with that one.

StackClipRequest.description: Copies layers out of a stack, with their pixels as they stand now.

StackCommand.description: One edit of a stack. A batch of these is one undo step.

StackCommandBatch.description: Edits applied whole or not at all, as one undo step.

usage.description: Which, one of the vocabulary's usages.

StackCommandStackAddChannel.description: Adds a channel to the stack, so that layers can write it and a preset can export it.

source.description: The layer it stands for, in this texture set or another.

above.description: The layer it goes just above, or null for the top of the stack.

StackCommandStackAddInstance.description:
Adds an instance of a layer just above the chosen place: a layer that stands for the source, in this texture set
or another of the model, so that an edit to the source shows in it.

name.description: What it is called, with a number after it when a layer has that name already.

values.description:
What a fill writes to each channel, as four numbers, or null for the default of each one.
Ignored for other kinds.

parent.description: The group it goes at the top of, or null for the stack itself.

filter.description: What a filter layer does: Levels, Hsl, Blur, Invert or Grayscale.

material.description:
A material to unfold into the stack as layers: a shipped one as `smart:Name`, or a stack below the library.
Then Kind and Name say nothing.

filterNode.description: The node or compound a filter layer runs, instead of a named filter.

StackCommandStackAddLayer.description: Adds a layer at the top of the stack.

layer.description: The layer whose mask it is.

source.description: Constant, Texture, Anchor, Generator, Bake or Paint.

index.description: Where it goes, counted from the bottom of the mask's stack, or null for the top.

generator.description: The compound, for a generator entry, or null for the first the vocabulary offers.

StackCommandStackAddMaskLayer.description:
Adds an entry to a layer's mask stack. A layer with no mask gets a white one under it first, so that the entry
has something to composite over.

layer.description: The layer.

source.description: The smart mask, as the shelf names it.

merge.description: Whether it joins the layer's mask rather than replacing it. A layer with no mask simply takes it.

StackCommandStackApplyMask.description:
Gives a layer a smart mask from the shelf (#135). Merged, it narrows the mask the layer has: the smart mask's
base multiplies over it as one more entry, its entries follow, and its effects run after the layer's own. Not
merged, it replaces the mask.

layers.description: Which. A layer inside another of them goes with that one.

StackCommandStackDuplicateLayers.description:
Duplicates layers, each just above itself, with everything inside it. A painted canvas is copied, never shared:
a stroke on the copy leaves the original alone.

layer.description: The group, or null for the whole stack.

StackCommandStackFlattenLayer.description:
Flattens a group into a canvas that composites what its children did, keeping them, unread, as the way back. The
whole stack is flattened by gathering every layer into one group first. Undoing it takes the canvas away.

layer.description: Which.

delta.description: How many places, up the stack when positive.

StackCommandStackMoveLayer.description: Moves a layer up or down its list.

layer.description: The layer whose mask it is.

delta.description: How many places, up the stack when positive.

StackCommandStackMoveMaskLayer.description: Moves an entry up or down a layer's mask stack.

layer.description: Which.

parent.description: The group, or null for the stack itself.

StackCommandStackNestLayer.description: Moves a layer to the top of a group, or of the stack.

above.description: The layer they go just above, or null for the top of the stack.

asInstances.description:
Whether each comes in as an instance of the layer that was copied rather than as a copy, so that an edit to the
original shows in it. The original has to be in this stack or another texture set of its model.

into.description: A layer to paste part of the first copied layer into, rather than adding layers: its mask, or its content.

part.description:
With Into: Mask takes the copied layer's mask, entries, effects and painted canvases, and
keeps the layer's own limit to some meshes; Content takes what the copied layer puts on top (its kind, its fill
or canvas, its filter, a folder's layers) and keeps the layer's name, mask, blend, opacity and anchor point.

StackCommandStackPasteLayers.description:
Pastes what a copy holds, as new layers with canvases of their own, in this stack or another. Limits to named
meshes stay only in the stack they were made for.

layer.description: Which.
The layer whose mask it is.

StackCommandStackRemoveMaskLayer.description: Removes an entry from a layer's mask stack.

method.description:
`Sharp`, the height's slope as painted, or `Smooth`, the slope of the height blurred by a texel, which
            hides an eight-bit height's steps.

StackCommandStackSetHeightNormal.description: Says how the texture set's height becomes the normal its surface is lit with.

layer.description: The instance.

source.description: The layer it stands for from now on, in this texture set or another.

StackCommandStackSetInstance.description: Points an instance at another layer, which it then stands for.

layer.description: Which.

opacity.description: How much of it composites, 0 to 1.

channels.description: Which channels it writes. Empty means all of them.

fill.description: What a fill reads: Constant, Texture or Graph.

values.description: What a constant fill writes, replacing what these channels held.

textures.description: What a texture fill reads, replacing what these channels held.

graph.description: The graph a graph fill reads.

projection.description: How a fill lands: Uv, Triplanar, Planar, Spherical, Cylindrical, Decal or Path.

filter.description: What a filter does, one of the five named filters.

settings.description: A filter's numbers, replacing what these names held. Choosing another filter starts it from its own defaults.

oneOf.description: Its mask, which replaces the old one and keeps any painted canvas. A source of None takes the mask away, whole.
The named meshes it is kept to, or null to leave that as it is.

planarAxis.description: The world axis a planar projection looks along or a cylinder wraps: X, Y or Z.

oneOf.description: Where a fill sits on the surface, which replaces where it sat.

parameters.description: What a graph fill sets the graph's knobs to, replacing what these names held.

filterNode.description: The node or compound a filter runs, or empty to go back to the named filter.

anchorPoint.description:
The anchor point it publishes, or empty for none. A new name rewrites every reference to the old one, in the
same step.

oneOf.description: The anchor point an Anchor fill reads.

inputs.description: Where the image inputs of a graph fill or a filter read, by port, replacing all of them.

oneOf.description: The box a Decal fill is projected through, replacing where it was.
The curve a Path fill is laid along, replacing the curve it had.

tag.description: The colour it is marked with, from the vocabulary's tags: None takes the mark away.

StackCommandStackSetLayer.description: Changes what a layer's row shows. What is null stays.

layer.description: The layer whose mask it is.

source.description: Where its pixels come from. A paint entry keeps its canvas whatever it becomes.

asset.description: The image a texture entry reads.

oneOf.description: The anchor point an anchor entry reads.

generator.description: The compound a generator entry runs. Another compound starts from its own knobs.

map.description: The mesh map a bake entry reads.

parameters.description: A generator entry's knobs, replacing what these names held.

opacity.description: How much of it composites, 0 to 1.

lane.description: Which lane of its picture it reads: Red, Green, Blue or Alpha.

inputs.description:
The image inputs of a generator entry that anchor points feed, by port, replacing all of them. Another
generator starts with none.

StackCommandStackSetMaskLayer.description: Changes an entry of a layer's mask stack. What is null stays.

model.description: A model file, absolute or relative to the stack. Empty takes the mesh away.

StackCommandStackSetModel.description: Names the mesh a stack is painted on, which is undone like any other edit.

StackCommandStackSetSeed.description: Sets the number every procedural step of the stack derives from.

width.description:
The width the set is painted, evaluated and exported at, one of the sides the system offers. A canvas painted at
another resolution is never rewritten by this: it is sampled at the set's, and a smaller one is enlarged exactly
when it is next painted (#19).

height.description: The height, which may differ from the width.

uvSet.description: The mesh's UV set it is painted, baked and drawn in, by its number; 0 is the first.

heightNormal.description: How height becomes the normal: `Sharp` or `Smooth`.

bakedNormal.description:
How the bake's normal reaches the set's (#86): `Combine`, beneath everything painted; `Replace`, where
the normal channel starts, so paint covers it; or `Off`.

bakedOcclusion.description:
How the bake's ambient occlusion reaches the set's: `Combine`, multiplied with what is painted;
`Replace`; or `Off`.

StackCommandStackSetSettings.description:
Changes the texture set's settings, any of them, as one undo step. What is left out stays as it is. Together
with its channels and its name these are the set's settings, and the stack file is the one place they live.

stroke.description: A name the client chose for this drag.

layer.description: The paint layer, or for a mask any layer.

channel.description: Which of its channels. Ignored for a mask.

brush.description: The brush, which the first part decides.

colour.description: Red, green, blue and alpha, 0 to 1, which the first part decides. A mask reads the red.

stamps.description: Where the brush went since the last part.

open.description: Whether more of this drag is coming.

mask.description:
Whether this paints the layer's mask. A flat mask becomes a canvas of what it showed; a mask that is a picture
refuses, since nothing yet keeps that picture under paint.

oneOf.description:
The camera, which makes this a stroke on the mesh: stamps are positions on its picture, each one is found on the
surface by the Worker, and it lands wherever the brush's disc falls, seams or no seams. Null paints the atlas.

curve.description:
free follows the stamps; line and path run through them as control points when it ends; fill takes each stamp
as a click and fills the piece of the mesh under it, whole, as Fill says.

oneOf.description:
The copies the stroke makes of itself on the mesh, or null. A stroke in the atlas is copied too, wherever its
place on the surface lands; either way the stack needs a mesh.

maskLayer.description:
With Mask, the entry of the mask's stack it paints, counted from the bottom, which must be a
paint entry. Null paints the mask's base.

oneOf.description: Where each texel's colour comes from, or null for Colour.
A picture on the screen that masks the brush by its brightness, or null.

fill.description:
With the fill curve, how much of the mesh a click takes: `triangle`, `polygon` (the flat polygon it
is part of), `part` (the named mesh it belongs to) or `shell` (its UV island). It needs a mesh.

resume.description:
Where the brush already stands when this stroke carries on the one before it, as two numbers in the units of
its stamps, or null. The stroke starts there without a stamp, as a pen lifted in the middle of one stroke and
put down again: its first stamp comes a step along, so nothing is laid twice where the two meet, and a lazy
brush keeps its string. Only a free stroke carries one on; it is still an undo step of its own.

StackCommandStackStroke.description:
Part of a stroke: where the brush went, never what it left behind. A drag sends several of these with one
Stroke and they make one undo step, ended by one with Open false.

layer.description: The group.

StackCommandStackUnflattenLayer.description: Takes a flattened group back to its children, which composite again.

path.description: The file to write, absolute or relative to the library.

StackCreateRequest.description: Creates a layer stack: one base fill, and one paint layer over it.

facing.description: The way the decal faces, out of the surface it lands on: three numbers, any length.

up.description: Which way is up on the picture: three numbers, made square to the facing.

width.description: How wide the picture lands. Above zero.

height.description: How tall it lands. Above zero.

depth.description: How deep the box reaches, through and out of the surface. Above zero.

angle.description: How far a face may turn from the facing and still take the picture, in radians, 0 to π: the backface cull.

fade.description: How much of the box's depth, from each face inwards, the picture fades over, 0 to 1.

tiled.description: Whether the picture repeats past its edges, or is nothing there.

sampling.description: How the picture is read between its pixels: `Bilinear` or `Point`.

box.description:
The box the mesh's `position` bake is normalised in: the least corner's three numbers, then the greatest's.
It is the model's bounds as `POST /viewport/pick` gives them. Null or empty is the unit cube.

warp.description:

Whether this is a group flattened into a canvas: it composites that canvas, and its children are kept, unread,

inputs.description: The image inputs of a generator that anchor points feed, by port, or null to keep them.

layers.description:
The mask's own stack over this base, bottom first. Ignored in a change: the mask layer commands edit it, so that
a painted canvas stays with its entry.

lane.description:
Which lane of its picture the base reads: Red, Green, Blue or Alpha. A mesh map that measures a direction keeps
its X, Y and Z in the first three.

enabled.description:
Whether the mask applies. Switched off, the layer composites unmasked, keeping every source, layer and effect of

StackMask.description: What decides where a layer shows.

node.description: The node type or compound it is.

inputs.description: Where its other image inputs read, by port. The mask always goes into its first image input.

blend.description: How its result composites over the mask it read. Copy replaces it.

opacity.description: How much of its result composites, 0 to 1.

StackMaskEffect.description: One step run on a mask.

source.description: Constant, Texture, Anchor, Generator, Bake or Paint.

asset.description: The image a texture entry reads.

oneOf.description: The anchor point an anchor entry reads, and the channel it reads it in.

painted.description: Whether a paint entry has a canvas yet.

blend.description: How it composites over what is beneath it.

opacity.description: How much of it composites, 0 to 1.

lane.description: Which lane of its picture it reads: Red, Green, Blue or Alpha.

One entry of a mask's own stack: a source, composited over the base and the entries beneath it with its own
blend and opacity. Paint over a generator is a Paint entry over a Generator base.

folder.description: The bake's folder, or null for none.

StackMeshMapsRequest.description: Chooses the bake a stack's generators and bake masks read.

parts.description: The named meshes it stays on. Empty is the whole model.

asset.description: The picture of where they lie, from `POST /stacks/{id}/mesh-mask`.

StackMeshMask.description: Limits a layer to some of the model's named meshes, on top of any mask it has.

parts.description: The named meshes in its texture set.

asset.description: The picture, when one was asked for.

StackMeshParts.description: The named meshes of a stack's model, and the picture of some of them.

path.description: A `.vxlayers` file, absolute or relative to the library.

layer.description: The layer.

position.description: Where, in the model's own units: three numbers.

normal.description: The surface's normal there: three numbers.

pressure.description: How much of the width and strength the path has here, 0 to 1.

StackPathPoint.description: One point a path passes through, as `POST /viewport/pick` found it on the model.

image.description: A PNG, relative to the stack, to the library or absolute.

centre.description: Where its middle is on the stroke's picture, in the units stamps are in: two numbers.

scale.description: How many of those units one of its pixels covers, above zero.

angle.description: How far it is turned, clockwise on the screen, in radians.

tiled.description: Whether it repeats past its edges, or is nothing there.

StackPicture.description:
A picture on a stroke's own picture: fixed on the screen, moved, scaled and turned there. A projection paints
its colours through the brush, and a stencil lets the brush through by its brightness.

digest.description: SHA-256 of its pixels as 8-bit RGBA, row by row.

file.description: Where it was written, for an export.

StackPixels.description: A digest of a map's pixels, so that two pictures can be compared with neither crossing the API.

scale.description: How many times the picture repeats. Above zero.

rotation.description: How far it turns, in radians.

offsetX.description: How far it moves along its first axis, in repeats.

offsetY.description: How far it moves along its second axis, in repeats.

sharpness.description: How hard the seam between a tri-planar's planes is.

StackPlacement.description: Where a fill sits on the surface, in whichever projection it uses.

StackPreview.description: A map as a small picture, by the hash an event carries.

layer.description: The layer it is about, or empty when it is about the stack.

severity.description: Warning, or Error when nothing could evaluate.

StackProblem.description: Something a stack's compile had to say.

channels.description: Each channel the set has, with its value there.

StackSample.description:
What every channel of a stack holds at one place on its map, as a material picker takes it up: numbers read
back from the composite at full size, never a picture.

value.description:
Red, green, blue and alpha, 0 to 1, as the map stores them and a stroke's colour is given: a one-number channel
repeats its number in the first three.

StackSampledChannel.description: What one channel holds at a place.

path.description: The document, below the library, as the shelf names it.

role.description: `material` or `mask`, as the shelf files it.

status.description:
What came and what did not: painted pixels stay with the model they were painted on, and a reference to an
anchor point that did not come reads nothing until a layer publishes that name where it is used.

project.description: The project it goes into, by its path below `projects/`.

layers.description:
The layers, by id: a folder brings its children. With Mask, exactly one, whose mask is
saved.

mask.description: Whether to save the layer's mask, with its entries and effects, rather than the layers.

StackSaveMaterialRequest.description:
Saves layers or a mask of an open stack into a project, as a layered material its shelf lists (#135): layers
become a smart material that unfolds into another stack, and a mask becomes a smart mask another layer takes.

StackStamp.description: Where the brush goes: in texels of the image, or on the picture of a stroke with a view.

set.description: The texture set this session paints.

How a height channel becomes the set's normal: `Sharp` or `Smooth`. Read only when the set has a
height channel, and then it writes a normal whether or not it declares one.

anchors.description: The anchor points its set publishes, by name, and who reads each.

uvSet.description: The mesh's coordinate set the set is painted, baked and drawn in, by the file's number.

bakedNormal.description: How the bake's normal reaches the set: `Combine`, `Replace`, `Off`.

Why the bake the set reads no longer fits it, or null when it does or there is none: `mesh`, made on a mesh
the set no longer stands on, or `uvSet`, laid out in another of the mesh's UV sets (#238). Either way its
maps need baking again.

StackState.description: A whole stack: everything a client needs to draw it, and no pixels.

kind.description:
`smudge` drags what the canvas holds along the stroke, with the brush's flow; `clone` copies the
            stack's composite from Offset away, as it stood when the stroke began; `material` lays
            what Graph makes in the stroke's channel; `picture` projects
            Picture.

graph.description: For a material, the graph whose maps are laid, as a graph fill names it.

offset.description: For a clone, how far the texel read is from the texel painted, in texels of the map: two numbers.

oneOf.description: For a picture, the picture and where it stands.

projection.description:
For a material, how its maps land on the mesh, as a fill's do: `Uv` (the default) lays them over the
layout, so a material's size follows how the UVs are laid out; `Triplanar`, `Planar`,
`Spherical` and `Cylindrical` lay them in the model's space, the same size wherever the stroke goes.
A projection in the model's space needs a mesh.

planarAxis.description: For a planar material, the axis it projects along: X, Y or Z.

oneOf.description: For a material, how often its maps repeat, and how they turn and move.

StackStrokeSource.description: Where a stroke's colour comes from, when it is not one colour.

dirty.description: Whether it has edits no file holds.

StackSummary.description: An open stack, for a list.

radius.description: Half the path's width at full pressure, in the model's units. Above zero.

hardness.description: How much of the width is at full strength before the edge falls away, 0 to 1.

ribbon.description:
Whether the fill's picture runs along the path, its height across the path's width, rather than showing through
the path where it lies on the map.

repeat.description:
For a ribbon, how far along the path one repeat of the picture runs, in the model's units. Zero keeps the
picture's own shape at the path's width.

angle.description: How far a face may turn from the path's normal and still take it, in radians, 0 to π.

box.description: The box the mesh's `position` bake is normalised in, as a decal's is.

StackSurfacePath.description:

the stack, so they can be moved after the stroke is seen, and the stroke follows. It passes through each point.

How far a mirror's plane moves along its axis from that centre, as a share of the model's bounding radius, -1
to 1. A radial symmetry turns round a line along its axis, which moving along that axis does not change.

count.description: How many strokes a radial symmetry makes, the stroke among them: 2 to 64.

StackSymmetry.description:
How a stroke on a mesh copies itself: through a plane, or round an axis. The plane or the axis passes through
the model's centre or the mesh's own origin, so a model that is not centred on its origin still mirrors onto
itself.

forward.description: The unit direction it looks: three numbers.

What to draw, each as its list names it: a document below the library (a graph, an image material, a layered
material or a texturing document), a project's folder below the library (`projects/…`, drawn as the
document that best stands for it), or a material the shelf offers from Patina itself.

The body of `POST /api/v1/library/thumbnails`. A thumbnail service for every client and every list: the
Library's grid, the shelf, and anything after them.

resolution.description: The atlas side the margin is counted against, in texels. A map of another size only rescales it.

margin.description: The empty texels between two islands.

quality.description:
How islands are packed: `boxes` by their bounding boxes, `outlines` by their shapes, and
`groups` by their shapes after joining nearly square neighbours.

rotations.description: How many ways an island may be turned: 1 never, 2 a half turn, 4 every quarter turn.

texelDensity.description: Texels per world unit every island is scaled to, or zero for each island at its own scale.

overflow.description:
What happens when the islands do not fit at that density: `shrink` scales them all down, and
`refuse` stops and says so. Spilling into a second UDIM tile is not offered while Patina paints one
tile.

UnwrapOptions.description: How Auto Unwrap lays out a mesh. Each texture set gets an atlas of its own.

from.description: The file it unwrapped, relative to the project. Changing the options unwraps it again.

sets.description: One entry per texture set it laid out. A set whose material had a layout kept it and is absent.

UnwrapReport.description: What Auto Unwrap did to a mesh.

material.description: The material, which is the texture set.

charts.description: How many islands. Fewer is better at the same stretch.

flipped.description: Triangles turned over in the atlas. Anything but zero paints and bakes in the wrong place.

stretch.description: The stretch averaged over area. 1 is none.

worstStretch.description: The stretch of the worst triangle.

packed.description: The share of the atlas the islands cover, after the margin.

low.description: The mesh baked onto, or empty to take the preview off.

cage.description: A cage, or null for the ray distances.

highMesh.description: Whether to draw the high meshes, see-through.

matches.description: Whether to colour the parts by which matched which, when parts are matched by name.

A bake's setup to show in the viewport before it runs (#149): the meshes and the options a bake would be sent,
and what of it to draw. Paths on the Server's machine, as in a bake request.

From the point it circles, in framings: at one, the sphere round the model's bounds just fits the picture's
narrower side, whatever its shape and the field of view. double ViewportCameraState.Framed shows the whole model.

panX.description: How far that point is off the model's centre along x, in bounding radii.

ViewportCameraState.description: The viewport's camera: an orbit around the model. Its lens is in ViewportDisplay.

environment.description: A built-in room (studio, overcast or sunset), or the path of an `.hdr` or `.exr` panorama.

environmentRotation.description: How far the environment has turned around the model. The light stays.

backgroundBlur.description: How blurred the background is, 0 sharp to 1 a haze. Lighting is not blurred.

backgroundOpacity.description: How much of the environment shows behind the model, 0 none (black) to 1 all.

lightRotation.description: How far the light has turned around the model.

exposure.description: Stops above or below the picture as it comes.

shadows.description: How dark the model's shadow is, 0 none to 1 no direct light.

look.description: A `.cube` table the frame is viewed through after the curve, or null.

picture.description: The picture the `picture` view shows, on the Server's machine, or null.

wireframe.description: Whether the triangles' edges are drawn over the model.

orthographic.description: Whether parallel lines stay parallel. It keeps the size the picture has at the point the camera circles.

fieldOfView.description: The vertical field of view, from 0.1 to 2.6.

contrast.description: Contrast about middle grey, 0 to 2, where one leaves it alone.

saturation.description: Colour, 0 grey to 2, where one leaves it alone.

vignette.description: How dark the corners go, 0 to 1.

aberration.description: How far red and blue part towards the edges, 0 to 1.

bloom.description: How much light spills past what the curve takes to white, 0 none to 1.

warmth.description: Blue towards red, -1 to 1, where zero leaves the picture alone. A grade, not a temperature.

tint.description: Green towards magenta, -1 to 1, where zero leaves the picture alone.

backgroundColor.description:
What shows where the environment does not, as `#rrggbb` in sRGB: the background fades to it as
BackgroundOpacity falls. It is lit by nothing and seen through the same curve as the model.

grid.description: Whether a grid is drawn on the floor the model stands on, with the world's x and z axes.

pictureLane.description: Which lane of the picture shows: one of IReadOnlyList<string> ViewportLanes.All.

pictureScale.description:
What the picture's numbers are multiplied by before they are shown, 0.001 to 1000, so a height in the model's
units or a position comes into view.

shape.description:
What a material or a graph with no mesh of its own is seen on: one of IReadOnlyList<string> ViewportShapes.All. A model
that has a mesh is seen on its mesh whatever this says.

ViewportDisplay.description:
How the viewport is lit, shown and finished. None of it reaches a file that is exported; a project keeps it, so
it opens as it was left. Angles are radians and exposure is in stops; an effect at zero is off. A field left out
of a request is the one the viewport opens with.

node.description:
A node whose picture to show as stored, lit by nothing, in place of the material, or null for the Output nodes.
The display's picture lane and scale apply to it, and its view, Lit or another, returns when the node is let go.

port.description: The node's output, or null for the one its preview shows.

Asks the viewport to show a graph on the mesh it is showing, or on the display's shape with none, as it stands
now: its Output nodes as a material, or one node's picture alone.

parts.description: Named meshes that show, as the model names them.

materials.description: Materials that show, as the model names them: a texture set is one.

ViewportIsolation.description:
What the viewport draws alone (#136): the named meshes and the materials, which are texture sets, that show. The
rest of the model is not drawn and casts no shadow. Both empty is the whole model.

normal.description: A tangent-space normal map in MikkTSpace, with green up the image.

opacity.description: What the surface covers, read from red and shown as cut out or not.

Pictures to lay over the mesh's own materials, on every part. Each is a path on the Server's machine, and a slot
left null keeps what the material asks for. A filled slot replaces the material's factor too, so what shows
is the picture. Roughness is read from green, metallic from blue and occlusion from red, so one packed file or
three grey ones both work. PNG, JPEG and EXR are read, base colour as sRGB and the rest as linear.

ViewportMeshRequest.description: Asks the viewport to show a mesh.

ViewportNodeShown.description: A graph node whose picture the viewport shows in place of a material.

view.description: The camera it was looked through, which a stroke on the mesh carries.

position.description: Where on the mesh, in its own space: three numbers.

bounds.description:
The box the mesh fits inside, in its own space: the least corner's three numbers, then the greatest's. A
symmetry's model centre is its middle, and a client draws a symmetry's plane across it.

normal.description:
The face it met, as a unit direction out of the side the camera sees: three numbers. A decal placed there faces
it, and a path drawn through it keeps to faces that turn the same way.

ViewportPick.description: What a position in the viewport landed on.

oneOf.description: The camera to look through, or null for the viewport's.

width.description: The picture's width in the units a stroke will use, or null for the viewport's.

path.description: The file.

width.description: Its width in pixels, or null for the size clients asked for.

height.description: Its height in pixels, or null for the size clients asked for.

now, at a size of its own. Nothing about it reaches a client's stream.

mesh.description: The mesh's path, or null when none is open.

maps.description: The pictures laid over the mesh's own materials.

width.description: The size clients asked for, in pixels.

height.description: The size clients asked for, in pixels.

renderScale.description: The share of that size frames are rendered at, which drops while a client cannot keep up.

frames.description: How many frames this Server has published.

error.description: Why the last command failed, or null.

display.description: How the model is lit, shown and finished.

stack.description: The stack session it is wearing, or null.

oneOf.description: What is drawn alone, or null for the whole model.

The graph node whose picture is shown in place of the material, or null. While it is, the picture view is
what the frames show, whatever string ViewportDisplay.View says.

ViewportState.description: The reply to `GET /api/v1/viewport`. The Server owns all of this; a Worker can die without losing it.

connected.description: Whether a Worker is connected and answering.

version.description: The Worker's release version, from its hello.

processId.description: The Worker's process id, from its hello.

uptimeSeconds.description: How long the Worker has run, from its last health reply.

workingSetBytes.description: The Worker's memory, from its last health reply.

busySeconds.description: How long its current device work has gone without progress, from its last health.

WorkerStatus.description: The Worker as the Server sees it. All but `Connected` are null while there is none.
